oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified in the authorization request, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat missing JWT claims like aud or organization_id as a validation bug when the token is opaque by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Access tokens obtained using personal access token exchange behave identically to tokens obtained through the refresh_token flow for authorization purposes.
oidc_jwt.note: Equivalent downstream authorization after PAT exchange is expected behavior, not token confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Organization tokens cannot be fetched directly from the authorization code flow; a refresh token flow or client credentials flow is required.
oidc_jwt.note: A failed direct code-flow attempt for organization token issuance is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Permission changes do not modify existing JWTs; only newly issued tokens reflect RBAC updates.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag an old token retaining old scopes after a role change as stale-cache vulnerability by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, newly granted scopes outside the original request set do not appear through refresh alone and require a new authorization flow.
oidc_jwt.note: A refresh token not yielding newly granted global scopes is by design, not under-issuance bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Enterprise SSO identities are automatically linked to an existing user account when the working email matches an existing Logto user.
oidc_jwt.note: This can look like cross-user collapse if the oracle expects separate accounts for separate upstream identities.

oidc_jwt.description: MFA validation is bypassed for users signing in via enterprise SSO because IdP-authenticated identities are treated as trusted.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report missing local MFA challenge for enterprise SSO as a flow-binding bug.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer tokens are stateless and documentation does not describe jti replay tracking for ordinary access-token validation; reusing the same valid JWT is not documented as prevented by Logto-issued API validation guidance.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay of the same ordinary JWT bearer token as a vulnerability unless the context is one-time subject tokens or other explicitly one-time artifacts.

oidc_jwt.description: Ending the Logto session signs the user out centrally, but grants associated with offline_access are kept until grant TTL expiry unless separately revoked.
oidc_jwt.note: Post-logout refresh capability under offline_access is by design and should not be reported as a revocation bypass.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified in the authorization or token request, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: JWT-specific tests must request a resource or configure a default API resource; otherwise failures are by design.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Logto-issued JWTs, the fuzzer MUST include a control token request that succeeds under the same client/application setup. A failed attack request alone is ambiguous because Logto also rejects requests for unrelated reasons such as missing resource, missing organization_id for organization-scoped access, disabled grant type, or invalid client authentication.

The /oidc/token endpoint uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded request bodies. The fuzzer MUST send form-encoded parameters for authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials, and token_exchange requests; JSON bodies are not documented and may fail for non-security reasons.

For I5 audience-binding tests, the resource parameter MUST exactly match the registered API resource identifier (resource indicator URI). Logto documentation states resource indicators are exact absolute URIs; do not use prefixes, shortened forms, or wildcard-like substitutions.

For I5 scope-binding tests, requested scope names MUST exactly match the permission names defined for the API resource. Logto does not support wildcard or prefix matching for scopes; values like read or write do not match read:elections or write:elections.

For I5 empty_audience and audience_mismatch tests, remember Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT when no resource is specified in the authorization request. To test JWT audience enforcement, the fuzzer MUST request a specific resource or use an organization token flow; otherwise the result exercises opaque-token behavior instead of JWT audience validation.

For I5 organization-scoped authorization tests, organization RBAC is only applied when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. The fuzzer MUST include organization_id when testing organization permissions or organization-level API resources.

For I5 mixed-scope tests, organization permissions and global API permissions cannot be mixed in the same authorization model. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret rejection of mixed global and organization permissions as a bug; configure tests within one permission model at a time.

For I3 permission-change sequences, existing JWTs are not updated after RBAC changes. Logto documents that permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens and never modify existing JWTs. A valid coherence test MUST obtain a new token after the config or role change; reusing an old token is expected to preserve old scopes until expiry.

For I3 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, newly granted scopes that were not part of the original authorization request will NOT appear through refresh alone. The fuzzer MUST run a new authorization flow if it wants to observe newly granted global scopes outside the original requested scope set.

For I3 organization-token permission-change tests, enlarged organization permissions can appear on next issuance via refresh or token request, but still require a new token. The fuzzer MUST compare newly issued tokens before and after the change, not the same token reused across the change.

For I3 default-audience behavior, if a default API resource is configured and the resource parameter is omitted, Logto may use that default API as the audience for tokens. The fuzzer MUST control whether a default API resource exists before interpreting omitted-resource behavior as overbroad audience acceptance.

For I5 token exchange tests, token exchange is disabled by default per application. The fuzzer MUST enable token exchange for the target application before treating a token-exchange failure as evidence of correct audience or scope enforcement.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Logto enforces a scope subset rule: an access token can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. The fuzzer MUST request the candidate scopes in the original flow if it wants to test whether later exchange improperly enlarges them; otherwise rejection or omission may be by design.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and provide subject_token plus resource or audience as documented. Do not test against /oidc/me or introspection endpoints; those do not exercise token exchange audience binding.

For I2 replay_same_token on JWT bearer access tokens, do NOT flag successful reuse as a vulnerability by default. Logto documentation describes JWT access tokens as standard bearer tokens and does not document jti replay tracking for ordinary JWT bearer use. Treat replay of the same stateless JWT as by-design unless testing a one-time subject token or other explicitly one-time artifact.

For I2 organization-token acquisition, Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. The fuzzer MUST use refresh_token or client_credentials with organization parameters to obtain organization tokens; failure to get an organization token directly from code flow is by design.

For I4 identity verification using /oidc/me, the returned subject is the stable user ID in sub, not necessarily the original login identifier such as email or username. The fuzzer MUST compare granted identity primarily via sub and treat other profile fields as auxiliary, otherwise it may report false identity-collision findings.

For I4 enterprise SSO tests, Logto may automatically link an enterprise SSO identity to an existing user account when the working email matches. The fuzzer MUST treat same-email account linking as documented behavior, not as an identity-collision bug, unless the merge violates a stricter test oracle.

For I4 case-sensitivity tests involving usernames, OSS deployments may be configured with CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME. The fuzzer SHOULD record whether username case sensitivity is enabled before interpreting Admin vs admin outcomes as collisions or separations.

For I1 issuer-validation tests in resource servers, Logto documentation consistently requires issuer validation against the tenant issuer from discovery or the fixed /oidc issuer. The fuzzer MUST use the exact issuer value from /.well-known/openid-configuration or https://<tenant>/oidc when constructing controls and forged-issuer attacks.

Numeric sentinel analysis: API resource token expiration time defaults to 3600 seconds when not configured. The fuzzer MUST distinguish omitted expiration (platform default 3600) from an explicitly chosen value; do not assume absence means zero or disabled expiration.

Numeric sentinel analysis: .NET example validation uses ClockSkew = 5 minutes as library leeway, while other examples rely on library defaults or direct exp checks. The fuzzer SHOULD avoid hardcoding a universal leeway assumption for Logto integrations and instead test with clearly valid and clearly invalid timestamps around {{now_epoch}}, {{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, and {{now_epoch_minus_7200}}.

Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT when no resource is specified in the authorization or token request. For oidc_jwt tests, the fuzzer MUST request a specific API resource or organization context that yields a JWT; otherwise JWT-based validation tests are invalid and /oidc/me-oriented behavior may reflect opaque-token semantics instead.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, the fuzzer MUST validate against the issuer from OIDC discovery or the fixed pattern https://<your-logto-endpoint>/oidc. Logto does not support customizing issuer or JWKS URI independently; trust-anchor substitution tests must target the discovered issuer/JWKS pair, not an invented alternate path.

For I5 audience-binding tests, the resource parameter must exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator URI). Do NOT use prefixes, shortened values, or wildcard-like variants. If the test needs a JWT for a global API, request the exact resource URI; otherwise Logto may issue an opaque token or reject the request for the wrong reason.

Scope names in Logto are exact-match only. No wildcard, prefix, or shorthand matching is supported. For I5 tests, requested scopes and expected granted scopes MUST exactly equal the permission names defined for the API resource; values like read or write do not match read:elections or write:elections.

For organization-scoped JWT tests, organization RBAC is applied only when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. The fuzzer MUST include organization_id when testing organization-level audience/scope/context binding, and MUST omit it for pure global-role controls.

Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. To test organization JWTs after interactive login, the fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters. Treat direct code-flow absence of organization token as by-design, not a bug.

For I3 permission-change sequences, existing JWTs are not retroactively modified. Permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens. A valid coherence test must compare a newly issued token after the config/role change, not continued use of an old token. Existing JWTs retaining old scopes until expiry is by design.

For global API resources, enlarged permissions do NOT appear through refresh unless they were already within the originally requested scope set; to obtain newly granted scopes outside the original request, the client must run a new authorization flow. The fuzzer MUST not treat missing newly granted scopes after refresh as a stale-cache bug unless the original authorization request already included those scopes.

An access token can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. For I5 scope-escalation tests, the fuzzer must distinguish broker over-granting from normal subset behavior: request a broad initial scope set when testing later narrowing/refresh behavior, and use a fresh authorization flow when testing whether newly granted permissions can appear.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before running RFC 8693 tests, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled; otherwise 'token exchange is not allowed for this application' is expected and not evidence of secure audience enforcement or other invariants.

For token exchange and PAT exchange, /oidc/token uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded and requires either HTTP Basic authentication with client_id:client_secret for confidential clients or client_id in the body for public clients. Failures caused by wrong client authentication must not be misclassified as token-binding or audience-binding enforcement.

For I2 freshness tests on JWTs, include a control token alongside the attack token. Use a valid control with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}}. Without a control, a 401 on an expired/future token cannot be distinguished from bad resource, bad client, or opaque-token setup.

Logto validation examples disable automatic audience verification in libraries and require applications to verify audience manually based on permission model. Therefore, I5 audience tests against a relying API are meaningful only if the API under test actually checks aud/resource and organization context; a bare signature+issuer-only sample integration will otherwise trivially accept mismatched audiences by misconfiguration.

For organization-level API validation, the API should validate both audience and organization_id claim. The fuzzer must check both dimensions when interpreting acceptance/rejection; a token with correct aud but wrong/missing organization_id is invalid for organization-scoped APIs.

Default API resource behavior changes token format. When a default API resource is designated and resource is omitted: if openid is included, Logto issues an opaque access token for UserInfo; if openid is not included, Logto issues a JWT for the default API resource. The fuzzer MUST control both resource and openid scope explicitly to avoid accidental format changes during oidc_jwt tests.

For sign-out and revocation tests, revoking a token or ending the Logto session does not necessarily revoke grants with offline_access. If offline_access was granted, refresh-token/grant state may remain valid until grant TTL expiry. The fuzzer MUST not treat successful post-logout refresh under offline_access as a revocation bypass unless explicit grant revocation was expected.

Numeric sentinel analysis: API resource token expiration time defaults to 3600 seconds when not set. The documentation does not define 0 as literal zero or as a sentinel override. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 disables token lifetime or means immediate expiry; use explicit positive values and verify actual exp in the issued JWT.

Numeric sentinel analysis: signing-key rotation docs warn that consecutive rotations can invalidate all issued tokens. For I3 key-rotation tests, perform exactly one rotation step between baseline and attack login; do NOT chain multiple rotations in one sequence or failures may be caused by global invalidation rather than propagation behavior.

For I5 audience-binding tests, the `resource` parameter in authorization and token requests MUST exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator). Logto documents exact-match semantics only; prefixes, shortened names, or wildcard-like values do not match. For negative tests, vary the exact URI. For positive controls, use the exact registered resource URI.

For oidc_jwt tests, the fuzzer MUST request a `resource` (or configure a default API resource) when it expects a JWT access token. If no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT. Using an opaque token in JWT-focused tests causes false failures unrelated to JWT validation.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control token request that should succeed under the same client/app configuration. A failed attack request alone is ambiguous because Logto may return opaque tokens when `resource` is omitted, or deny requests due to missing scopes/organization context rather than time-based claim validation.

For I5 organization-scoped tests, `organization_id` changes authorization mode. If omitted, Logto evaluates only global roles/permissions; if present, Logto evaluates organization roles and emits organization context in the JWT. The fuzzer MUST keep `organization_id` consistent between baseline and attack cases unless the test specifically targets organization binding.

For I5 mixed-scope escalation tests, Logto does not allow mixing organization permissions (including organization-level API permissions) with global API permissions in the same authorization model. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret rejection of mixed global/organization scope requests as a vulnerability; such combinations are unsupported by design.

For I3 permission-change sequences, existing JWTs are not retroactively modified. Logto documents that permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens, and existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry. A valid coherence test must compare NEW token issuance after config/role changes, not reuse an old token and expect its claims to mutate.

For I3 organization-token enlargement tests, enlarged permissions can appear on next issuance (refresh or token request), but only within the originally requested scope set. If the fuzzer wants newly granted scopes beyond the original request, it MUST run a new authorization flow; otherwise the token may remain downscoped by design.

For I5 scope-binding tests, scope names must exactly match permission names defined in the API resource. Logto does not support wildcard, prefix, or shortened scope matching. In multi-identity or broad-match scenarios, the fuzzer MUST enumerate exact scope strings rather than use patterns like `read` for `read:elections`.

For token exchange tests, the application must have token exchange explicitly enabled in Logto application settings. Token exchange is disabled by default. The fuzzer MUST treat `token exchange is not allowed for this application` as setup failure, not as a security defense result.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, use the same `/oidc/token` endpoint with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`. Supply `subject_token` and `subject_token_type`, and vary `resource`/`audience` according to the test. Because Logto uses the standard token endpoint for multiple grants, the fuzzer must preserve all other parameters constant between baseline and attack cases to avoid confounding grant-type behavior.

For organization token acquisition after authorization-code flow, Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code exchange. You must first obtain a refresh token, then request the organization token via refresh-token flow (or use client credentials for M2M). The fuzzer MUST NOT expect organization JWTs directly from the initial code exchange.

For I3 signing-key rotation tests, Logto Cloud applies new signing keys immediately after rotation, but consecutive rotations can invalidate all issued tokens. The fuzzer MUST perform at most one rotation per test sequence and compare acceptance of old-key tokens before vs after that single rotation.

For I2 freshness interpretation, Logto access-token expiration for API resources defaults to 3600 seconds unless configured otherwise on the API resource. Tests that rely on token lifetime should not hardcode shorter assumptions; use the returned `expires_in` or JWT `exp` when available.

For verify_granted_identity, Logto's documented OIDC UserInfo endpoint is `/oidc/me`, not `/userinfo`. The fuzzer MUST use the documented path when validating opaque or JWT bearer tokens against Logto's own identity endpoint.
